question.prompt: What entry URL should runnable web tests use for the storefront and checkout flow?

options.label: Use {{start_url}}
options.detail: Author the tests with a {{start_url}} placeholder until the real storefront URL is provided.

options.label: Provide URL
options.detail: Replace the placeholder with the actual storefront URL before running the tests.

content.risk_rationale: Without a starting URL, no web test for this checkout can run even if the assertions are otherwise complete.

question.prompt: What concrete checkout data should runnable successful-order tests use for guest details, delivery details, and payment?

options.label: Use variables
options.detail: Author the tests with variables such as {{guest_name}}, {{guest_email}}, {{delivery_address}}, and {{payment_details}} until real test data is supplied.

options.label: Provide data
options.detail: Replace the variables with a real test customer, address, and payment method before running the tests.

content.risk_rationale: A successful guest-checkout test cannot be executed without concrete purchaser, delivery, and payment data or approved variables.

content.text: Checkout completion does not require account sign-in or registration.

content.text: A successful order shows an order confirmation to the customer.

expected_answer.operand: order confirmation after a successful order

content.text: A successful order confirmation includes an order number.

expected_answer.operand: order number on the order confirmation after a successful order

content.text: A successful order is sent to Sarah by email.

expected_answer.operand: the successful order in an email sent to Sarah

content.text: Delivery date selection does not allow Sundays.

expected_answer.operand: a successful end-to-end guest checkout on a phone-sized web surface

judgements.rationale: [risk_factors] Applied money because blocking guest checkout blocks order capture; user-reach because one-off buyers are the primary audience in the source; change-frequency because checkout gating often changes with form or account-policy updates.

[risk_factors] Applied money because confirmation proves the purchase path completed; data-loss because a missing confirmation can hide a lost order; user-reach because every guest buyer depends on this end state.

[risk_factors] Applied money because the order number is needed to identify a captured purchase; data-loss because losing the identifier makes follow-up and reconciliation brittle; user-reach because every successful buyer receives this surface.

[risk_factors] Applied money because Sarah receiving the order is how fulfillment starts; data-loss because a missing email can mean a lost order despite customer payment; user-reach because every placed order relies on staff receipt.
[risk_factors] Applied money because invalid delivery-date selection can create unfulfillable orders; change-frequency because date-picker rules often move with operating schedules.
